title: Hosting a short-term rental in Hawaii: county rules, seasons and salt air
summary: Hawaii vacation rental rules by county, visitor seasons, inter-island logistics and a salt-air maintenance checklist, with official sources.
body_markdown:
[All posts](https://prohost.ai/blog)


**Hosting in Hawaii means four counties with four sets of rental rules, a visitor year that peaks in July and December, every replacement part arriving by ship or plane, and salt air that eats metal. None of it is a reason not to host there. All of it is a reason to set up the operation differently from a mainland rental. This guide covers the rules by county, the seasons, and the operations that are specific to the islands, with sources, as of November 19, 2026.**


## Key takeaways


- **Rules are county by county.** Oʻahu limits stays under 30 days to resort areas and units with a nonconforming use certificate. Maui is phasing out apartment-district rentals by 2029 and 2031. Hawaiʻi County started registering every short-term rental in September 2026. Kauaʻi allows them only in Visitor Destination Areas.
- **The taxes are the same everywhere and you file them yourself.** 11% state TAT, 3% county TAT, and GET you can pass on at up to 4.712%. As of November 19, 2026, Airbnb doesn't collect them in Hawaii, so for Airbnb stays you register, charge, file and pay; on Vrbo, Booking.com and other channels, check the platform's current tax settings. Full detail in our[Hawaii taxes guide](https://prohost.ai/blog/hawaii-short-term-rental-taxes-and-county-rules) .
- **The visitor year is steady, with July and December on top.** Hawaii had 9.64 million visitors in 2025 ([DBEDT](https://files.hawaii.gov/dbedt/economic/tourism/monthly-highlights/press-release-2025-12.pdf) ).
- **You need people on the island.** State law requires a local contact who lives on the same island as the unit. Plan your cleaner, handyman and backup the same way.
- **Salt air is a maintenance schedule, not a surprise.** Rinse, keep humidity down, and keep dissimilar metals apart, per the University of Hawaiʻi corrosion lab.

## Where we're coming from


We host in Hawaii, the Smokies and Joshua Tree. Of the three, Hawaii is where the rules move fastest and where a broken part takes longest to replace. Before ProhostAI I spent 6 years at Airbnb as a staff data scientist on the hosting team, and Hawaii was always one of the markets where the gap between a well-run listing and an average one showed up clearly in reviews. Most of that gap is operations, which is what this guide is about.


## The rules, by county


Every county regulates where you can rent for less than 30 days. The state taxes the stay on top. Here is the short version. The[taxes and county rules guide](https://prohost.ai/blog/hawaii-short-term-rental-taxes-and-county-rules) has the forms, rates and links.


County Where stays under 30 days are allowed What changed recently


Oʻahu (Honolulu) Resort districts, certain registered apartment areas, or with a nonconforming use certificate 90-day minimum elsewhere (Ord. 22-7); federal injunction protects pre-existing 30-89-day rentals; registration renews yearly


Maui Hotel and resort zoning, permitted short-term rental homes, and (for now) apartment-district units on the Minatoya list Bill 9 (2025) ends apartment-district rentals by Jan 1, 2029 (West Maui) and Jan 1, 2031 (rest of county); new H-3/H-4 hotel districts may exempt rezoned buildings


Hawaiʻi County Depends on zoning and existing permits Ordinance 25-50: every rental of 180 days or less must register; registration opened September 2026


Kauaʻi Visitor Destination Areas, plus listed nonconforming rentals and approved homestays No rule changes 2024-2026; renewals by certified mail with no grace period


Two rules apply statewide. Every ad must show your TAT registration ID and a local contact, and the same information must be posted inside the unit ([HRS 237D-4](https://files.hawaii.gov/tax/legal/hrs/hrs_237d.pdf) ). And since Act 17 (2024), any county can phase out or set minimum stays of up to 180 days in any zoning district ([Act 17](https://data.capitol.hawaii.gov/sessions/sessionlaws/Years/SLH2024/SLH2024_Act17.pdf) ). If you're buying, read the county page for your exact parcel and assume rules can tighten.


## The seasons


Hawaii's visitor year is flatter than most mainland markets, but it isn't flat.


- **2025 total:** 9,642,991 visitors, down 0.6% from 2024, spending $21.75 billion, up 5.7% (preliminary,[DBEDT, January 29, 2026](https://files.hawaii.gov/dbedt/economic/tourism/monthly-highlights/press-release-2025-12.pdf) ).
- **Peaks:** July and December are the top months in DBEDT's monthly releases. In 2025, July had 873,430 visitors and December 868,894.
- **Softer months:** April and May, and the fall after Labor Day, run lower. That's our reading of DBEDT's monthly releases, not a DBEDT statement.
- **Maui is still recovering from August 2023.** Maui visitors fell 57.8% in August 2023 after the Lahaina fire. In 2025 Maui had 2,516,163 visitors, up 7.0% on 2024 ([DBEDT](https://files.hawaii.gov/dbedt/economic/tourism/monthly-highlights/press-release-2025-12.pdf) ).


What this means for a host: holiday weeks and summer sell early and at the top of your range. Use[dynamic pricing](https://prohost.ai/integrations/pricelabs) so April and October don't sit empty at summer rates, and use gap-night[upsells](https://prohost.ai/features/upsells) to fill the one-night holes between longer winter stays.


## Operations that are specific to the islands


### Everything arrives by ship or plane


A replacement dishwasher, a washer part, a bed frame: on a mainland rental it's a next-day delivery. In Hawaii it's often a barge. Inter-island freight runs through regulated water carriers, including Young Brothers, whose rates and tariffs are set by the state Public Utilities Commission ([PUC water carriers](https://puc.hawaii.gov/water-carriers/) ). On the neighbor islands, plan on longer waits than you're used to.


What to do about it:


- **Keep spares on the island.** A second set of linens and towels per bed, a spare smart lock or keypad, a spare thermostat, filters for every AC unit, the light bulbs your fixtures use, and the one washer or dryer part that fails first.
- **Buy appliances you can get serviced locally.** A brand with a technician on your island beats a better appliance that has to be shipped back.
- **Keep an inventory list per unit.** When something breaks at 9 p.m., whoever is on call needs to know whether the spare is in the closet or at another unit.


### You need people on the same island


State law requires your local contact to live on the same island as the unit ([HRS 237D-4](https://files.hawaii.gov/tax/legal/hrs/hrs_237d.pdf) ). Treat that as the minimum. A working Hawaii operation needs, on the island:


- A primary cleaner and a backup cleaner.
- A handyman who can do small plumbing and electrical.
- An AC technician, because a unit that stops cooling in August can't wait for a mainland part.
- A pest-control service on a schedule.
- Someone who can be at the door within an hour for a lockout.


If you're looking for local help, the[ProhostAI vendor directory](https://prohost.ai/vendors) lists cleaners, handymen and other service providers by city, including[Honolulu](https://prohost.ai/vendors/honolulu-hi-us) ,[Maui](https://prohost.ai/vendors/maui-hi-us) ,[Kihei](https://prohost.ai/vendors/kihei-hi-us) and[the Big Island](https://prohost.ai/vendors/hawaii-hi-us) .


### Salt air is a maintenance schedule


The University of Hawaiʻi at Mānoa's corrosion research lab has studied this for years. Its advice for homeowners is short: sea salt is very corrosive, so wash it off; keep indoor humidity under 60%; and keep dissimilar metals, like brass and galvanized steel, apart ([UH Mālamalama](https://hawaii.edu/malamalama/2004/05/f7_corrosion.html) ). Turned into a rental schedule:


```text
HAWAII SALT-AIR MAINTENANCE CHECKLIST (oceanfront or ocean-view unit)


Every turnover
[ ] Wipe door handles, lock keypads and sliding-door tracks with fresh water
[ ] Rinse the grill and wipe it dry; cover it
[ ] Check screens for tears (they let salt spray and bugs in)


Monthly
[ ] Rinse lanai furniture, railings and outdoor fixtures with fresh water
[ ] Check smart lock batteries and the keypad for corrosion or sticky keys
[ ] Run dehumidifier or AC dry mode; check indoor humidity (target under 60%)
[ ] Clean AC filters; check the outdoor condenser fins for salt build-up


Quarterly
[ ] Lubricate door hinges, sliding-door rollers and lock mechanisms
[ ] Inspect outdoor electrical covers, light fixtures and outlets
[ ] Have the AC units serviced (coil cleaning, drain lines)
[ ] Check for rust where different metals touch (brass on galvanized, etc.)


Yearly
[ ] Replace corroded hardware with stainless or marine-grade parts
[ ] Repaint or reseal exposed metal railings
[ ] Replace outdoor electronics (cameras, sensors) showing corrosion


```


Smart locks deserve their own note. A keypad that sticks in salt air is a lockout at 10 p.m. Keep a spare, keep a backup code, and check the keypad every month.


### Water, sun and pests


- **Sand:** an outdoor shower or foot rinse saves your floors, your washer and your septic or sewer line.
- **Beach gear:** say exactly which beach towels, chairs and umbrellas you provide in the[guidebook](https://prohost.ai/features/guidebooks) , so guests don't have to ask.
- **Pests:** ants, roaches and geckos are part of island life. Guests accept geckos; they don't accept roaches. Pest control on a schedule is cheaper than refunds.

## FAQ


**Can I run a Hawaii rental from the mainland?** Yes, if you have a local contact on the same island, a cleaner and a backup, and a handyman. The law requires the local contact. The rest is what keeps your reviews up.


**What's the best island to start on?** The one where you can legally rent your specific property. Zoning decides more than demand does. Read the county rules for the exact parcel before anything else.


**Do I need to collect taxes if I only rent a few weeks a year?** Yes. TAT and GET apply to every transient stay. See the[Hawaii taxes guide](https://prohost.ai/blog/hawaii-short-term-rental-taxes-and-county-rules) .


**When is high season?** July and December are the top months by visitor count. Holiday weeks book earliest.


**How do I keep salt air from ruining things?** Rinse metal with fresh water, keep indoor humidity under 60%, keep dissimilar metals apart, and replace hardware with stainless or marine-grade parts as it fails.


## The takeaway


Hawaii rewards hosts who plan for it. Check your county's rules for your exact property first. File the three taxes yourself. Staff the island, not just the unit. And put salt-air maintenance on a schedule before the first keypad sticks. The rest of hosting, the messages, the cleanings and the reviews, works the same way it does anywhere, and that part can run on software.
